answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before bidding. A whisper of fraud is not enough to seize it: a verifiable rule violation, such as submitting a forged receipt, triggers a public dispute and slashing. A prism of many fake identities then offers no cheap camouflage, because each one needs its own locked capital. If the fakes cheat and are caught, the attacker loses those stakes rather than merely a plume of disposable accounts.
